A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LongVALE benchmark and LongVALE-LLM. Their main text, seven tables, fifteen figures, equations, and supplementary sections are available and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongVALE evaluations, zero-shot audio-visual question answering results, ablations, and event-boundary analysis in Tables 2-7.

after.justification: v3 retains the original evaluations and analyses in Tables 2-7 and additionally quantifies the manual annotation-checking outcome in Section 7.3.

M1.justification: The filtering, event-boundary detection, and correlation-aware captioning pipeline is unchanged. LongVALE-LLM retains the same encoders, adapters, Vicuna backbone, and boundary-perception and instruction-tuning stages.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LongVALE corpus and three fine-grained tasks, plus AVSD and Music-AVQA for zero-shot evaluation. The added ACAV row in Table 1 describes an already-used data source and does not establish additional experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 retain their respective comparator sets, including TimeChat and VTimeLLM for LongVALE and OneLLM and AVicuna for AVQA. ACAV's addition to the descriptive dataset comparison is not an evaluated model baseline.

E3.justification: The 7,240/1,171 training/test split, 585/586 easy/hard subsets, metrics, model configurations, training schedule, and evaluation prompts are unchanged. Newly disclosed manual-check counts describe the existing annotation workflow without establishing a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same training-stage, audio-visual correlation, and modality ablations in Tables 4-6, boundary-coherence analysis in Table 7, and qualitative cases in Figures 5 and 12-15. Section 7.3 quantifies existing manual checking without introducing a separate error-analysis study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice and random sampling described for Table 7 remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 7.3 newly reports approximately 300 annotation errors corrected during checking of 2,000 videos, adding a limited audit outcome. All performance, ablation, and boundary-analysis values in Tables 2-7 remain unchanged, including 54.8 on AVSD and 49.4 on Music-AVQA.

T1.justification: The Max Running Semantic Difference definition in Equation 1 and multimodal token-concatenation formulation in Equation 2 are unchanged. No assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: the annotation pipeline, approximately 8.4K videos and 105K events, three omni-modal tasks, and improved temporal and cross-modal understanding. The new resource-access statement does not redefine these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of modality contributions, correlation-aware captions, generalization, and future work remain unchanged. The risk-mitigation paragraph moves from the main-text conclusion area to supplementary Section 11 without substantive additions.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project URL and states that the dataset and code are available. Section 7.3 newly specifies 2,000 manually checked videos, three minutes per video, and 115 total human hours. These extend documentation; existing hyperparameters, hardware, and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v3 removes citations to Spatial-temporal Pyramid Graph Reasoning for Action Recognition and UniAV, and adds ACAV to Table 1's benchmark comparison. The central positioning against coarse-grained and visual-only approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits include author-affiliation and corresponding-author information, a small wording correction, added disclosure sentences, and relocation of risk mitigation into Section 11, renamed Broader Impact. The overall narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a video-count column and an ACAV row. Existing main-text figures receive limited font and spacing adjustments, with local table and text reflow. The appendix figures and experimental displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency and usability through explicit dataset/code access information, quantified annotation-checking effort and corrections in Section 7.3, and dataset-scale context in Table 1. These address limited documentation gaps while preserving the methods and empirical evidence; they do not substantially strengthen the paper's scientific validation.
